EU student fees UK changed at a fixed point, and pre-Brexit advice no longer applies. This guide covers the current rules for the 2027/28 entry cycle, the costs to expect, the exceptions that may grant home fees, how the four UK nations differ, scholarships, and how to confirm your own status before accepting an offer.

University fees for EU students in the UK: the quick answer after Brexit

Brexit moved most EU students from the regulated home rate to the open international rate, and the cutoff was a course start date.

Anyone who started a course in 2020/21 or earlier kept their eligibility for the rest of that course. So university fees for EU students after Brexit depend on when your course begins and what status you hold.

Quick answer: a new EU, EEA or Swiss student starting in 2027/28 without a recognised home-fee category will usually pay international fees. Settled or pre-settled status may support a home-fee assessment only when the relevant residence and other eligibility conditions are also met. Always ask the university to confirm the decision in writing.

Home fee status vs international fee status

The two fee categories sit far apart on cost, and the gap is the main reason your fee-status assessment matters.

Home fee status means you pay the regulated home rate. In England, the maximum standard full-time undergraduate fee for 2027/28 is £10,050 at providers permitted to charge the maximum rate. EU students receive this rate only when they fall within a recognised home-fee category.

International fee status means the university sets the fee itself. International fees for EU students UK are not capped, so two universities can charge very different amounts for similar courses. Establish your fee category first, then compare the exact 2027/28 course fees.

Why EU students should not rely on nationality alone

An EU passport feels like it should settle the question. It does not.

That is why two EU nationals with identical passports can receive different fee status assessment UK outcomes, depending on residence, settled or pre-settled status, course start date and family circumstances. The home-fee criteria themselves are set in government regulations, and UKCISA’s full list of home-fee categories for England sets out how each route is met. Treat your passport as one input, then check the other two.

How much are UK tuition fees for EU students?

There is no single figure: fees can range from England’s £10,050 maximum home rate to international fees above £60,000 a year for some clinical courses.

UK tuition fees for EU students vary by university, course, study level, subject and fee status. For 2027/28, the maximum standard full-time undergraduate home fee in England is £10,050. As a current UK-wide benchmark, the British Council gives international undergraduate tuition fees of approximately £11,400 to £38,000 a year and postgraduate fees of approximately £9,000 to £30,000.

These international figures are broad planning ranges, not guaranteed 2027/28 prices. Always check the official fee page for your exact course and entry year.

Undergraduate and postgraduate EU student fees

Undergraduate and postgraduate pricing follow different logic, and conflating them leads to bad budgeting.

For international students, undergraduate fees for EU students UK are usually set per course and held fairly steady across the years of study, subject to annual increases. Postgraduate fees for EU students UK are often more variable, shifting with subject, university reputation, course length and location. A one-year master’s in a high-demand subject can cost far more than a broader taught course elsewhere. Pull the specific course page for your start year, not a sector average, and build the annual increase into your plan.

High-cost courses EU students should check carefully

Some subjects carry fees that dwarf the typical international rate, and the list is predictable.

Medicine, dentistry, veterinary science, engineering, lab-based science, business and MBA programmes sit at the top end because of facilities, placements and clinical training.

Medicine is the clearest high-cost example. Current published figures include an international/EU MBChB fee of £54,650 per year at the University of Edinburgh for 2026/27, while the University of Oxford lists overseas fees of £49,400 for pre-clinical study and £65,250 for clinical study.

Many universities had not yet confirmed their 2027/28 international medicine fees by 2 August 2026. Do not carry an earlier intake’s fee into a 2027 budget unless the university states that it will remain unchanged. Across a five- or six-year degree, tuition alone can exceed £200,000. Check every year of the course and read our guide to studying medicine in the UK for international students.

Settled status, pre-settled status and residence rules

Status alone is rarely the whole test; residence usually decides the outcome.

Scholarships and cheaper options for EU students in UK universities

A scholarship will not change your fee status, but it can cut the bill that fee status sets.

Several UK universities run EU-specific scholarships, EU fee discounts, international merit awards or country-based awards. These are university-specific and shift by intake, course and year.

The University of Portsmouth is a useful example: its EU Scholarship has been extended to the 2028/29 intake, with separate eligibility for undergraduate and postgraduate applicants and a residence condition. Postgraduate eligibility is limited to applicants who meet Portsmouth’s specified nationality and domicile conditions, so the scholarship does not apply automatically to every EU, EEA or Swiss student.

Cheaper choices can also move the total: lower-cost cities, shorter courses, part-time options, the earning value of a placement year, and comparing course-level fees across universities. Treat each award as one line in a wider cost comparison, not the deciding factor.

How EU students should compare scholarships

A high headline value can still leave you short, so compare the conditions, not the number.

Check the award value, the duration, whether eligibility is automatic or application-based, any course exclusions, the renewal rules and the deadline.

A scholarship may reduce your fee and still leave a large remaining cost, especially on high-fee courses where a fixed discount covers a small share. The right comparison is full cost minus scholarship value, not the scholarship value on its own.

How to confirm your exact EU student fee before applying

Reading a guide is the start; confirming your own number is the finish. Work through these steps in order:

  1. Check the official course fee page for your exact course and start year.
  2. Read the university’s EU or international fee-status guidance.
  3. Check UKCISA’s fee-status guidance and run its fee-status self-check.
  4. Where your status is unclear, ask the university for a written fee-status assessment before you accept an offer.
  5. Compare scholarships against the full fee before you accept an offer.

Documents to have ready before you apply:

  • Passport or national ID.
  • EU Settlement Scheme share code.
  • Proof of settled or pre-settled status.
  • Three-year residence history.
  • Previous study records.
  • The university’s fee-status questionnaire.
  • Parent or family-member status documents, if relevant.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do EU students pay international fees in the UK?

In most cases, yes. New EU, EEA and Swiss students starting in 2027/28 will normally pay international fees unless they qualify under a recognised home-fee category.

Can EU students still get home fee status in the UK?

Sometimes. Settled or pre-settled status, Irish citizenship, protected citizens’ rights, worker status and qualifying family-member categories may lead to home fees when the relevant residence and other conditions are met.

Are EU students with settled status eligible for UK university home fees?

They may be eligible, but settled status alone does not guarantee home fees. The decision also depends on residence history, the applicable fee-status category and the UK nation where the university is located.

Are university fees for EU students different in Scotland?

The available fee-status categories are different. Most new EU students without a qualifying Scottish category pay international fees. Scotland’s funded home tuition is based on residence and fee-status rules, not simply on holding an EU passport.

Do UK universities offer scholarships for EU students?

Many universities offer EU-specific scholarships, international merit awards or tuition fee discounts. The value, eligibility requirements, exclusions and duration vary by university, course and intake.

Can my fee status change after I start university?

Sometimes, but not automatically. Whether you can move from international to home fees during a course depends on the regulations of the relevant UK nation and whether you enter a qualifying category. Ask the university for a written reassessment before relying on a fee change.

Conclusion

Before accepting an offer, check the university’s official 2027/28 course fee, request a written fee-status assessment and compare available UK university scholarships with the total tuition cost.
